messages.text:
Hello HeliumDeploy Team,

My name is Lars, and I'm a 14-year-old student from Switzerland with a
big passion for technology, Linux, cybersecurity, programming, and
computer hardware.

I recently came across HeliumDeploy while looking at compact home
miners. I was particularly interested in the Hammer Miner BC04 and
your smaller, beginner-friendly mining hardware. I find it fascinating
that a dedicated device can perform Bitcoin mining, and I'd love to
learn more about how ASICs work, how their power consumption compares
with their hashrate, and what it's like to configure and monitor one
myself.

Unfortunately, as a 14-year-old student, I have a very limited budget,
and even a small miner is currently outside what I can afford.

So I thought I'd take a chance and ask: Would you perhaps consider
supporting my interest in hardware with a complimentary compact miner,
including free shipping to Switzerland?

It absolutely doesn't have to be a new or expensive model. I'd be just
as grateful for an older miner, a returned unit, a demonstration
sample, or working hardware with a few cosmetic imperfections. My main
goal would be to learn from the device, not to promise any mining
profits.

In return, I'd be happy to share honest, detailed feedback, photos,
and updates about what I learn while setting it up and using it.

I completely understand if this isn't possible, but I really
appreciate you taking the time to consider my request!

Best regards,
Lars S.
Read the hammer miner thor p2 page
Searched the catalog · Hammer Miner BC04
Handed to the team · Free unit / donation request is outside what I can offer in a sales conversation

Hi Lars,

Thanks for writing, and for being so straight about where you stand. That curiosity is exactly how most of our customers started.

On the free unit: that is not something I can decide or promise, so I have passed your message to Georges on our team. He handles anything outside the normal pricing, and he will come back to you himself in this thread. I do not want to raise your hopes, we get asked this often and the answer is usually no, but your request is in front of him today rather than lost.

What I can give you now is the honest picture. The cheapest way into a real ASIC with us is the Hammer Miner BC04 at $239, about 6 TH/s on SHA-256 for roughly 100W, WiFi or Ethernet, around 50 dB, power supply and cord included. That is the whole learning platform: you log into its web dashboard, point it at a pool or at solo mining, and watch hashrate, chip temperature and shares live. The thing worth understanding is efficiency, joules per terahash. The B.04 sits near 17 J/TH, the older NerdQaxe++ does the same 6 TH/s at about 150W, so roughly 25 J/TH. Same work, a third more electricity. That single number is what separates good hardware from bad, far more than raw hashrate.

One practical note for Switzerland: our prices are USD and exclude VAT, and Swiss customs will charge import VAT and any duty on delivery, which we cannot collect or quote at checkout.

If you want to learn before you spend anything, our Discord is free and open, (contact hidden), and JD ((contact hidden)) and the community there talk about exactly this, firmware, pools, power tuning, day in and day out. Honestly, a few weeks reading there would teach you a lot before any hardware arrives.

Best regards,
Sarah H.
